contentBlocks.text: You've compared decimals. Today: round them to a given place!

Rounding a decimal works just like rounding a whole number: look at the digit right after the place you're rounding to. If it's 5 or more, round up; if it's less than 5, round down. To round 3.14159 to the nearest hundredth, look at the thousandths digit (1) — since it's less than 5, round down, giving 3.14. Round 6.782 to the nearest tenth.
You just rounded decimals to a given place! Tomorrow we'll add and subtract decimals in real word problems.

objectives: Round a decimal to a given place using the standard rounding rule
Correctly round 6.782 to the nearest tenth
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's place-value and comparison work.
2. Model rounding 3.14159 to the nearest hundredth.
3. Have the child round 6.782 to the nearest tenth independently.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's decimal-addition lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: underline the place being rounded to, then circle the digit right after it, as a consistent visual routine
Ready for more: ask the child to round the same number (6.782) to the nearest hundredth instead, and compare the two results
This connects directly to whole-number rounding taught in earlier grades — point out the rule works exactly the same way
teacherGuide.answerKey: 6.782 rounded to the nearest tenth is 6.8 (the hundredths digit, 8, rounds the 7 up to 8).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 5 standard 5.NBT.4: using place value understanding to round decimals to any place, continuing this week's decimal thread.

generationData.instructions: Round each decimal to the given place.
